title: Automorphisms of punctual Hilbert schemes and symmetric powers of varieties: the descent lemma for equivariant automorphisms
author: Ashima Bansal, Supravat Sarkar, Shivam Vats
work: Automorphisms of punctual Hilbert schemes and symmetric powers of varieties
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Lemma (source0.tex lines 772--774, source label open): for smooth curves with the second projective, an equivariant automorphism of the m-fold product of the product curve over the m-fold product of the base curve that fixes the small diagonal pointwise either descends to an automorphism of every partial product, or the number of factors equals two and the automorphism factors through the product of the curve with the base; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 777--889 (one adjacent proof environment of 113 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span together with its retained context. It argues by induction on the number of factors, reduces to the case of two factors using the retained product-automorphism lemma, analyses the commutative diagram describing where the automorphism sends the partial products, splits into the cases in which the image of a partial product is a partial product of the same type or of the complementary type, uses the retained corollary on automorphisms without unit components to control the induced automorphisms of the base curve, and then shows in the exceptional two-factor case that the automorphism has the prescribed factored form; the final steps identify the translations and bundle automorphisms realising the factorisation. This lemma is the structural step on which the article's classification of the automorphism groups of punctual Hilbert schemes and symmetric powers rests, and its proof is a complete research-level algebraic-geometry argument. H2: a research-level algebraic-geometry lemma whose proof combines a product-automorphism structure theorem, an induction over the number of factors, a case analysis of the images of partial products and the classification of automorphisms without unit components on a curve; it is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
